Add observations to an mt_data object

Source: R/data-mt_data.R
mt_add.Rd

Add observations to an mt_data object

Usage

mt_add(
  data,
  measure,
  x,
  by = NULL,
  age = "age",
  period = "year",
  value = NULL,
  age_open = NULL,
  missing = c(".", "..", "...", ":", "x", "X", "/", "NA", ""),
  zero = "-",
  decimal = "."
)

mt_add_deaths(data, x, ...)

mt_add_exposure(data, x, ...)

mt_add_population(data, x, ...)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

measure

One of "deaths", "exposure", "population".

x

A data frame in long format.

by

Character vector of stratum columns (for example "sex").

age

Age column: one column with single ages (numeric) or labels such as "30-34" and "90+" (see parse_age_labels()), or two columns with the lower and upper bound (Inf for an open interval).

period

Period column: calendar years (numeric), labels such as "2010-2014", or two columns with lower and upper bounds.

value

Name of the value column.

age_open

Lower bound of an open age interval coded as a single numeric age (for example 110 for the Human Mortality Database "110+").

missing

Values that mark missing cells in character value columns, for example the symbols of official statistics for confidential or unknown counts (".", "x"). Missing cells are left out; suppressed death counts can then be estimated with mt_fill_suppressed().

zero

Values that mark a count of zero (for example "-").

decimal

Decimal mark of values given as text: "." (thousands separators such as "12,345" are recognised) or "," (as in many European exports: "1.234,5").

...

Arguments passed to mt_add().

Value

The updated mt_data object. An existing table for the same measure is replaced.

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = 2001, age = 30:31, deaths = c(5, 7), exposure = c(9e3, 9e3))
x <- mt_add_deaths(mt_data(), d)
x <- mt_add_exposure(x, d)
x
#> <mt_data> 1 stratum, omega = 110
#>   deaths     single years 30-31; periods 2001-2001 (width 1); 2 cells
#>   exposure   single years 30-31; periods 2001-2001 (width 1); 2 cells
#>   grid       <mt_axis: age, 2 intervals> 30 31
#>              <mt_axis: period, 1 interval> 2001
